Fallout 4 and what we currently know.
With the announcement of Fallout 4 and all the hype with it, I am reminded that I have no idea about this franchise and wonder why people are so crazy about it. Please explain (like I'm 5), thanks.
ELI5: What is the big deal with the Fallout franchise?

It's been around for a long time and has a lot of lore behind it, much like the Elder Scrolls (Skyrim) series. They both have a lot of open world roaming and freedom and that appeals to many people - though obviously Elder Scrolls is fantasy and Fallout is post-apocalyptic, so the vibe is very different.

I've only given the series a cursory look, wasn't a big fan, so that's the best explanation I can give. I wish I could get into them more, since the storylines I've seen from poking around the Fallout wiki a bit seem pretty cool.
I didn't realize that Bethesda made it. I love Skyrim, I've decided to buy F4 and give it a try (once it's out of course). Thanks.
Play Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas while you're waiting

Bethesda games in general have a massive following due to Elder Scrolls and Fallout. People (me included) love the truly open non-linear gameplay as you can literally do anything you want and can be expanded, customized and enhanced by player-created mods.

Also, there is an absolutely ridiculous amount of content and lore that adds an amazing amount of depth to the gameplay.

It's possibly one of the most well written pieces of gaming I've ever encountered. In addition to it's non linear gameplay, you're faced with moral, political, and psychological decisions while being immersed in a world eerily similar to our own, but following a different timeline.

The lore behind it is immense. It's like discovering another society. Every single thing is integrated to this alt universe and well written. Each faction has a unique story, each character/follower you meet has an independent personality and your decisions affect how much of their lives they reveal to you, thus opening side quests that make the game have a different outcome.

In a world of anarchy, war, and hellish creatures, you're faced with the question: Is man really good?

I could go on forever about these games. I love them so much. It's fucked up, frightening at times, and suddenly you're immersed in this world where your actions directly affect the well being of the NPCs and the world around you.

You explained it on an emotional level better than I could ever. It's hard to describe. Start a new game in the morning and after a blink of the eye it is 3am. Man I miss those days with Skyrim, FNV and FO3.
It still happens to me. I get way into my characters. God i am PUMPED for FO4

It's an 18 year old franchise of games where you could do almost anything and do it with violence. It wasn't the first of it's kind but it's become the best and most famous non-linear post-apocalyptic role playing game.
I really regret no one really creates games like old Fallout series (1,2).

It's like asking what's the big deal with the Star War franchise. It's a world that many, many people just envelope themselves in. And care deeply for the lore and characters. And being the interactive medium that video games are, just completely immerses you into this post-apocalyptic word. With hundreds of things to do and even more people to talk to.

Bethesda games:

The world itself is alive. Day and night cycles, etc... but, the NPCs also have their own lives. They have daily scheduals that they follow. They sleep at night, they go to work in the morning, etc. You can interact with them and they all react differently based not only on who they are and what they do, but also who you are... both 'good' and 'bad' and also depending on your characters stats like intelligence or charisma.

All characters have places where they work and live. You can totally rob them. Break into their home and steal the items in their house. Or, break into their place of work at night and rob the store while everyone is asleep. In Morrowind games, you can even become a vampire...at which point you break in to peoples homes at night, and bite them while they sleep.

All of the objects in these games are interactive. Stores actually have items on the shelves. So while you do shop through a list, the list is derived from what is actually on the shelf. You can totally knock items off the shelf or when you steal an item, it actually does dissapear from the shelf. You can then place this item where you want... kind of like Minecraft in a weird sort of way.

Everything is like this though. Every peice of food, every plate on every table, ever piece of silverware... swords, guns, ammo, trash, etc.

All characters are people with stats and equipment. You can pickpocket NPCs and take the change or the keys to their home from their pocket. If you steal their hat, the NPC itself is no longer wearing a hat. If you max out the skill, you can literally rob the clothes off peopls back... making them walk around in their underwear. Pointless, but fun.

Same goes for bad guys though. You steal the armor they wear... the guns they use. No bad guy attacks you with a super gun that can't be looted. Either he has a super gun or he does not. If you have a spell that can knock that gun out of his hands, the gun itself will literally fall onto the ground and you can just pick it up and use it.

The maps are huge and the detail in the environment is crazy good. There are little untold stories everywhere you look. Sometiems it's just a skeleton sitting at a table with an empty cup and a bottle of poison. Or you'll find a skeleton hand with a ring under a rock... I guess he was crushed? These things are everywhere... every building has a story or 10 to tell, even without actual quest logs.

Then there is the story and quests. Main story quests, side story quests, strange story quests... all of which give rewards and have multiple steps to complete. You'll earn sidekicks or random weapons... you can build a home, and you can even decorate your home with the prizes from these quests. You can get dummies, and then put the armor sets you colelcted on the dummies... or just any random piece of armor you want. You can have display cases that you can fill with any item, you can hang whatever you want, etc...

In skyrim, one sick bastard would save and then load his game, kill an NPC and hope he got the "beheading" animation. Since the heads are objects, he would pick them up, take them to his house, and put the heads on his shelves. He would also drag the headless bodies inside and set them in chairs at his dinner table.

Any character that isn't necessary can be killed. So if you want to kill a shop owner and rob the store, fucking do it.

There are also lots of ways to complete quests... characters with high charisma/intelligence can sometimes talk their way out of a fight. The higher the charisma the more chat options you have when talking to people. It works opposite too... people with low intelligence will have few chat options... sometimes things that don't even make sense.

"How long you been in town"?

-- Ugh! -- Pizza! -- You cow.

so you can play the game over and over and over again and it'll play differently depending on character stats or what order you do quests. Since the game is open world you can do just about anything at any point in time.

There are also quests that don't even really exist. In Fallout 3 there was a building that no quest took you too that had no quest tied to it. But exploring the building kicked in a haunting. Things would fly off the shelves or the lights would burn out. You would see shadows move and ghosts lurk around the corner or whatever. Explore enough and you could uncover why it was haunted... eventually finding a dark secret in the basement. Again, all of this... and no quest. No reason to ever go to this building except for the fact that you were just walking around looking at stuff.

The game is designed well... you can Roleplay easily if that's what you're into. Want to just rush through the game... quick travel is a thing. Like to take your time, walking from place to place is filled with beautuiful sights and lots of random encounters. some rarer then others, some funny.

There's a random encounter in Skyrim where a wizard tries to fly and blows himself up... or something.

You can join guilds and become the leader, always taking on an infinte amount of randomly generated quests. Again, in skyrim, as leader of the theives guild, you could always do a "steal" quest. They would tell you to steal a random item from a random NPC in the game... how you stole the item was up to you... you could do these forever.

And that's just off the top of my head, I'm sure I'm missing things. Doing jobs to earn money, customizing gear, etc...

In short, they're the best games ever.

i don't trust ms this much, how *free is this upgrade? and any expected side effects or should i just man up and sign the deal? i'm on windows 7 which i'm very happy with but i understand ms won't support it forever and eventually i'll have to upgrade.
should i reserve a copy of windows 10 or wait?
I plan to wait, I really didn't want to let go of my xp but I have 8.1 now. It's not as bad as people said it would be (since they added the start menu back).

Here's a nice overview: http://www.windowscentral.com/windows-10-questions-and-answers-you-need-know-upgrading

All the "reservation" does is download the new OS to your system over the few days/week before the release date so that come July 29th, you aren't sitting in the same download queue as a million other people. It's just a way for Microsoft to distribute the load of millions of users downloading the new OS.

In terms of the quality of Windows 10, i've been using the preview for several months on my main computer and there are very few niggles with it (just UI polish) and i've never had a compatibility issue. It's pretty much rock solid, and runs noticeably quicker than W7.

The upgrade is "free" because MS never make much money from OS upgrades, so they're not losing out on much by offering it, and because it's easier and better for their vision of security and single app platform to have as many users on W10 as possible. The more people on W10, the more appealing the W10 store and environs are for developers.

If you're still unsure though, just sit it out a few weeks, wait for some solid reviews, for people you know to use it and tell you what they think, then download it through Windows Update. You do have a year, after all, to download it for free.
To piggy back off of this, most universities will have a free download of Windows 10, so if you are a student or know a student save your money

Yes, most Universities are enrolled in Microsoft DreamSpark, and you can pretty much get a load of free software, as well as Github Education Pack, and a few other things free just by providing your .edu email address.

As best as I understand you can reserve it and never use it. I don't believe you're forced to install it when it's released. Whether or not you upgrade is your choice. Your computer won't upgrade in the middle of playing LoL or something. So all in all - there's no reason NOT to reserve it. It's just a Windows Update item you can hide and ignore until you're ready.
